# I. THE CYCLE
[italic]Copied out of the paper notebook. Entries are counted in shifts since the case came in.[/italic]
## Shift 2. The egg Leathery, knee high, sat in the case like it had grown there. No shell in the bird sense. Warmer than the room. The skin takes a slow pulse when you stand close and goes still when you step away. I logged it as a dormant plant body.
[color=#7D7763]Put that on the record as my first mistake.[/color]
The crown is four lips pressed shut in a cross. They opened when Okafor leaned over it with the camera.
## Shift 2, later. The one that grips Out faster than I can write it. Finger legs, a long tail, a ribbed sac of a body. It went for the face, not the throat. Tail round his neck, legs locked behind his skull. We could not cut it off. See page II for why.
His pulse stayed steady. It was feeding him air. It wanted him alive.
## Shift 3 It let go on its own and died on the floor, curled up like a spider in a cold room. Okafor woke hungry and making jokes. The scan showed something under his sternum the size of my thumb. I told the clinic it was a cyst.
## Shift 4. The one that comes out At dinner. Pale, legless, all head and teeth, out through the ribs and away under the cabinets before anyone at the table had stood up. Okafor died in under a minute. The liaison had the room sealed before I finished washing my hands.
## Shift 6 to 11. The adult A shed skin in the vent above the lab, the length of my arm. Another on shift 9, too big for the duct it was found in. On shift 11 I saw the thing that left them, standing at the end of corridor C. Taller than me. A long smooth skull with no eyes I could find, and it did not need any.
From thumb to that in a week. It does not eat what we eat. I have not found what it eats yet.
[bold]Egg. Grip. Burst. Adult. One host per egg, and the host never survives it.[/bold]
